source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check Bios could be update via serial port
1. Make the connection between serial port and client.Up
2. Use command to update bios to newest version.
3. Restart the SUT and check the bios version.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Make sure bios could be update successfully.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: BIOS image + serial cable/client (operator); biosupdate tool
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Bios update: updating the BIOS via the serial port requires a physical serial connection to the client plus running the BIOS update over that serial console; the agent cannot physically attach the serial cable.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: operator connects the serial port, runs the BIOS update command to the newest version, restarts the SUT and checks the new BIOS version; agent cannot physically attach the serial link.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: BIOS update over serial re-flashes BIOS firmware; operator-only with the approved image, do not auto-run.

original_test_intent: Update the exact platform BIOS through its approved serial-console firmware path and verify the approved target BIOS version plus boot/platform health after restart.
original_method: An engineer establishes the validated physical serial path; after owner-supplied identity/image/tool/recovery validation and approval, the exact update is executed, the SUT restarts, and pre/post BIOS/version/settings/health evidence is compared.
manual_activity: An engineer must attach/validate the serial cable/client and supervise the physical recovery boundary. Once that environment is established and the exact plan is approved, the firmware command, transcript capture, restart and electronic verification can be automated.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/board/current BIOS and approved target version; never merely 'newest'
Signed image, hash, release notes and compatibility/upgrade path
Vendor updater/version/exact command/prompts and serial electrical/pinout/baud/protocol
Stable power, maintenance approval, settings backup, OOB/KVM and known-good recovery/reflash procedure
safety_requirements: Do not connect an unknown serial electrical path or execute an unverified firmware command.
Do not flash until image identity, signature/hash, compatibility, stable power and recovery are proven.
Never interrupt power/transport, clear evidence or auto-retry a failed flash.
Stop on any identity/signature/transfer/POST/settings mismatch and preserve the complete transcript.
agent_execution_scope: Perform read-only board/current BIOS/settings/health inventory and validate supplied artifacts/tool plan.
After physical setup and one approval, execute only the unchanged validated command while capturing the full transcript and power/restart timeline.
Verify exact target version, settings, POST/OS/BMC/SEL health and report Tool Result separately.
engineer_actions: Provide/approve the target manifest, serial procedure and recovery plan.
Establish the physical serial connection and remain available for hardware recovery.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly refuses an invented command, but physical connection alone does not make the whole case manual-only.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the platform-owner validated vendor updater and exact serial command; no generic modernization is safe or justified.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Serial update, restart, BIOS version check and 10/5-minute fields remain; 'newest' is retained as source text but requires an exact approved target before execution.

modernized_recommendation.status: VENDOR PROCEDURE REQUIRED; DO NOT SUBSTITUTE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a signed firmware manifest binding board identity, current/target BIOS, image hash, updater, serial settings, command/prompts, stable-power controls and recovery; then run one approved transaction and compare pre/post settings and health.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the exact board/BIOS/update path in the validated manifest.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record every image/tool/firmware version and hash.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Board vendor/FAE update and recovery documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the previously implicit target, transport and recovery contract explicit without replacing serial update.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; successful version change alone is not overstated as full health.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Complete vendor manifest and recovery proof.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A valid flash can still reset settings or fail boot; recovery remains engineer-controlled.

project_override_considerations: A project selects an exact target/version and may define upgrade or downgrade intent. Missing firmware artifacts make the execution not ready, not permanently BLOCKED. Any approved alternate update path is a disclosed project method and does not rewrite the serial master source.
expected_evidence: Board/current-target BIOS manifest, signed image/hash, tool/serial parameters and approval
Complete update transcript/status and controlled restart/POST
Exact target version, settings/non-target-change comparison, platform health, Tool Result and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: 'Newest' and 'use command' are unsafe placeholders but not contradictory. They require exact owner-supplied values before execution and remain preserved as source facts.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The operation and target category are clear. Under locked V3.1, missing package/tool/project parameters are readiness gates; manual serial setup followed by automatable core execution is PARTIAL, not permanent BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retain no-guessed-command and firmware risk boundaries.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retain every safety prerequisite but reject permanent BLOCKED for missing vendor inputs.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Adopts the later feedback re-review and locked readiness rule while preserving physical setup, no auto-retry and engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Avoids both unsafe generic flashing and over-blocking a well-defined firmware-update class whose exact vendor parameters can be supplied per project.
independent_technical_reasoning: Physical serial setup is mandatory, but after it the validated flash transaction and evidence capture are automatable. Missing exact firmware inputs affect readiness; they do not make the library intent unknowable, so the classification is REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION.
